Hello, I'm Hannah, and I write film reviews for a magazine in London. People often ask me about my favorite scene in a period drama. It's a dinner scene. A big family was having dinner in their country house. It was raining outside, and the candles were burning on the table. Everybody was talking and laughing. Then, while the father was telling a story, a servant came in with a letter. The father read it, and his face changed. Nobody said a word. The plot of the whole series changes in that moment. And no, I won't tell you what the letter said. No spoilers!

Hi, I'm Mike. I never liked period dramas. Then, two years ago, I was flying from New York to London at night. Everybody was sleeping, but I couldn't sleep. I was looking for a film, and I chose a period drama because it was the longest one. Big mistake, I thought. But after twenty minutes, I was crying. The main character was a young woman in the 1800s, and she was fighting for the right to study. While I was watching the last scene, the plane landed. The woman next to me said: you were crying, sir. I said: it's the costumes. They're beautiful.
